label: Figure 11.4: Short-run losses in perfect competition
alt: The firm takes price P and produces at q where MC = MR, but average cost C at q is above P, so the shaded rectangle between C and P is a loss.
caption: The firm sells at the market price P and maximises profit (here, minimises loss) at q where MC = MR. At q the average cost C is greater than P, so it makes a loss of (C − P) per unit, shown by the shaded rectangle. It still produces because P covers average variable cost, so producing loses less than closing.
